findings.issue: No test for the explicit-Save happy path on a COMPLETED step: the 'exact repro' test (L345-367) drives 'update:steps' (the implicit autosave path on the page) and asserts the PATCH fires. But it does not drive 'step-save' afterwards to exercise the full explicit-Save code path (onCanvasStepSave → stepSaveFeedback = null). The feedback-clear branch in onCanvasStepSave() is untested: if that branch were accidentally deleted, no existing test would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a fourth test in the describe block: mount with a completed step, emit 'update:steps' (triggers PATCH + clears feedback if any was set), then emit 'step-save' on that same completed step, and assert (a) storeMock.update was called exactly once (not twice), (b) wrapper.find('[data-test="funnel-step-save-feedback"]').exists() === false. This locks down the 'completed step → explicit Save → no duplicate PATCH, no stale feedback banner' invariant.

summary: All six required scenarios are covered by load-bearing, value-based assertions. The core repro (id:null node, 'Привіт' text, index routing) is tested at two layers (canvas unit + page integration). Saved-node regression, feedback-on-incomplete, no-PATCH-on-empty, and dangling-trigger tests all carry concrete assertions that would fail against pre-fix code. One minor gap: the explicit-Save happy path on a COMPLETED step (the feedback-clear branch in onCanvasStepSave) is not exercised, leaving that branch without a regression guard.
